item.text: {"question_id":"5B.7","answer":"The record supports formal disclosure, audit, monitoring, and correction mechanisms, but not reliable evidence that information was consistently independent, candid, or used to correct failure. Official reports documented fiscal execution, information requests, audits, debt-risk monitoring, exposed accountability cases, performance evaluations, and some corrective actions (BATCH-0003-E005; BATCH-0003-E010; BATCH-0007-E006). Xi-era directives also called for risk monitoring, institutional reform, supervision, and rectification, although the cited material does not establish independent oversight or successful implementation (BATCH-0004-E001; BATCH-0004-E002). The 2023 financial-work conference acknowledged persistent financial risks, corruption, weak service to the real economy, and weak regulatory capacity, but the supplied passage does not identify a specific subsequent remedy attributable to Xi (BATCH-0004-E014). The zero-COVID reversal shows policy change after mass protest, but its motivation is unresolved and does not demonstrate evidence-based evaluation; no official investigation into the policy’s handling was reported, while accountability efforts were repressed (BATCH-0001-E014; BATCH-0007-E013; BATCH-0022-E015). Censorship of economic reporting and manipulation of information around Xi’s reappointment further qualify claims of open, reliable evaluation (BATCH-0001-E014; BATCH-0021-E016). Thus, evidence indicates administrative monitoring and some correction capacity alongside materially constrained independent scrutiny, adverse-result disclosure, and accountability.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E010","BATCH-0007-E006","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E014","BATCH-0001-E014","BATCH-0007-E013","BATCH-0022-E015","BATCH-0021-E016","BATCH-0008-E010"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Official disclosure, audit, and performance systems do not establish reliable statistics, independent evaluation, or publication of adverse findings.","The supplied evidence does not show whether identified fiscal, financial, or program failures were corrected successfully, nor establish Xi’s personal response to each audit finding.","The zero-COVID reversal followed protest and political pressure; whether evidence-based monitoring contributed is unresolved.","The absence of an official investigation does not exclude a non-public internal review.","The evidence concerns mainly 2023 and adjacent late-2022/early-2024 periods, with limited direct measurement of economic-policy correction within the target year."],"corrections_made":["Removed the draft’s unsupported characterization of official information as reliable and of audits as independent evaluation.","Recast zero-COVID reversal as policy change under unresolved motivation rather than evidence-based correction.","Gave greater weight to censorship, information manipulation, the absence of an official zero-COVID investigation, and repression of accountability efforts.","Corrected attribution and causal limits for institutional reports and the October 2023 financial-work conference.","Preserved formal monitoring, audit, disclosure, and correction mechanisms as material but qualified support."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Independent replication or validation of official economic statistics is still missing.","Evidence of concrete post-audit remedies and their outcomes would materially clarify correction capacity.","Independent evidence on whether internal reviews occurred after zero-COVID is unavailable in the supplied record."]}
